title: Sentinel smoke overlay and performance heuristics for LTS rollouts
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal:
Build a lightweight, reproducible 'Sentinel' overlay runner that combines smoke checks, KV cache warmup probes, and performance heuristics to validate LTS-targeted runtime rollouts before traffic ramp. This ticket implements the orchestration and gating logic for cohort-aware validation cohorts, dynamic thresholding based on baseline fingerprints, and deterministic rollback scoring.

Why this differs from existing preflight rigs:
- Focused on LTS channel rollouts where stability requirements are strict; thresholds should adapt to golden baselines per-model and per-sequence-length cohorts.
- Lightweight overlay: runs fast shadowed workloads (no customer traffic mutation) and emits compact fingerprints for the release gate system.
- Heuristics-first approach: increases sensitivity to tail latency regressions and KV cache warmup regressions that are common in quantized/compiled builds.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Sentinel overlay runner service (stateless orchestrator) that instantiates validation cohorts and schedules: smoke probes, cache-warm probes, and synthetic perf traces.
2) Cohort definitions and fingerprinting: sequence-length buckets, model size class, and hardware profile. Store golden fingerprints in S3-backed manifest.
3) Dynamic gate evaluator: compares fingerprint deltas to cohort-specific thresholds and produces a human-readable gate summary + rollback score (0-100).
4) Telemetry hooks to Console: per-route fingerprint diffs, tokenized cost delta, tail-p99/p999 latency deltas, GPU util and memory pressure traces.
5) Runbook and automation: automatic canary hold if rollback score > 40, auto-notify #releases Slack channel, link to playbook for manual triage.
6) CI integration: a pipeline job that runs Sentinel against release candidates for runtime-1.20 and publishes artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sentinel runner can complete a full cohort pass within 12 minutes for the standard LTS smoke profile.
- Gate evaluator flags a known synthetic p99 regression (created by an intentional kernel slowdown) with a rollback score >= 60 in test runs.
- Console displays cohort fingerprint diffs and a single numeric rollback score for each candidate.
- CI job triggers on release candidate builds and uploads artifacts to the release bucket with stable naming.
- Runbook validated with SRE and assigned on-call for the rollout window.

Out of scope:
- Full chaos/latency injection harness (we will reuse ENG-88291 for chaos work).
- Full canary traffic ramp automation (this ticket provides the gate signal; the rollout engine will consume it).

Implementation notes and risks:
- Fingerprint stability: need deterministic synthetic traces and KV warmups; will pin seeds and use fixed prompt sets to reduce flakiness.
- Threshold tuning: start with conservative thresholds from historical LTS runs; add opt-in aggressive tuning for dedicated releases.
- GPU metrics: rely on existing exporter (ENG-10824) but add perf counters for memory fragmentation and PCIe stall heuristics.
- Flaky tests: include a flaky-detector stage to mark signals that require re-run vs immediate rollback.
